description:
Dünya için çözümler, uzay için vizyon.

Biz Eternal Fire ; yazılım, mühendislik, tasarım ve uzay bilimlerine tutkuyla bağlı, sınırları zorlamayı seven bir ekibiz. NASA Space Apps Challenge’da küresel zorluklara yenilikçi, açık kaynaklı ve sürdürülebilir çözümler üretmek için bir araya geldik. Amacımız sadece bir proje geliştirmek değil; veriyi anlamlı kılmak ve geleceğin uzay ve dünya teknolojilerine yön vermek.
summary:
We developed Mars EVA Mission Control & Survival Guide, an interactive 2D/3D web application (with English and Turkish support) for planning astronaut surface walks within 3 km × 3 km zones in Mars's Gale Crater (Mount Sharp) and Jezero Crater.

Our system converts NASA JPL Mars Trek 3D DEM terrain meshes into 15-meter resolution elevation, slope, and crater-depth layers. Using Curiosity REMS, Perseverance MEDA, and Curiosity RAD baselines, it models hourly solar shading, crater cold traps, and radiation exposure. An A* pathfinding algorithm calculates safe outbound and late-hour return routes, providing step-by-step navigation, battery and oxygen budgets, and alternative approach paths when terrain is blocked.

On Mars, the geometrically shortest path can trap astronauts in steep craters or freezing shadows, draining suit power. By comparing safe routes against blind shortest paths, our tool helps prevent critical resource depletion and supports astronaut survival.
details:
*Purpose & Benefits
In Martian extravehicular activities (EVA), the geometrically shortest route is often dangerous. Steep crater walls, freezing shadowed depressions, and late-day temperature drops can rapidly drain an astronaut's suit battery and oxygen. The purpose of Mars EVA Mission Control & Survival Guide is to calculate safe, survivable round-trip walking routes between a lander and scientific targets within hyper-local (3 km × 3 km) zones in Gale Crater (Mount Sharp) and Jezero Crater. Its main benefit is quantifying survival budgets (time, Wh battery, O2, and radiation) before an EVA starts and proving why avoiding hazards saves energy and lives compared to a blind shortest path.

*What It Does & How It Works
1. Terrain Pre-processing (`data_prep.py`): Parses raw NASA JPL Mars Trek 3D DEM surface meshes (.stl) into 200 × 200 grids (15 m per cell), preserving XY/Z proportions to extract elevation, slope angle, crater depth, and geological classes.
2. Physics & Survival Modeling (`survival_model.py`): Uses Curiosity REMS (Gale) and Perseverance MEDA (Jezero) 24-hour temperature curves plus Curiosity RAD baseline radiation (~0.64–0.66 mSv/day). For any selected Sol hour, it dynamically computes solar elevation/azimuth shading (hillshade), crater cold-air trapping, and optional 4x solar storm surges.
3. Multi-Criteria A* Pathfinding (`pathfinder.py`): Builds a dynamic cost grid that blocks impassable slopes, deep craters, and temperatures below suit limits. It calculates separate outbound and late-hour return routes (+5 hours cooling), turn-by-turn compass directions, and a blind shortest path benchmark.
4. Interactive Interface (`app.py`): Displays 2D/3D Plotly maps, battery/temperature telemetry charts, downloadable Markdown mission guides, and English/Turkish language switching.

*Factors Considered
Our team accounted for Martian gravity (3.72 m/s²), suit and equipment mass (150–195 kg across Standard EVA, Heavy Scientific Equipment, and Rover-Assisted profiles), uphill climbing potential energy, base life-support power (180 W), active thermal heating wattage, oxygen duration, topographic radiation shielding, and time-of-day cooling on the return walk.

* Creativity & Edge-Case Design
Instead of treating a Mars map as a static 2D distance problem, our tool combines offline NASA terrain geometry with real-time diurnal physics so outbound and return paths adapt to changing shadows and temperatures. Additionally, when terrain or extreme cold blocks a mission, the failsafe solver does not simply fail: it maps the closest reachable point (purple path) and calculates the exact minimum slope or crater tolerance needed to complete the route.

*Tools, Languages, Software & Hardware Used
- Programming Language: Python
- Framework & Deployment: Streamlit, Streamlit Community Cloud
- Libraries: NumPy, SciPy (`ndimage`), Pandas, Plotly, Pillow, `numpy-stl`, `tifffile`

- Collaboration & Design: GitHub, Canva, Gamma AI (presentation & slide design), standard developer laptops/PCs

- AI Assistance: Google Gemini (code refactoring, optimization assistance, and bilingual documentation) and Gamma AI (presentation structuring and slide drafting)
